Approaching a 4.0, the level of intensity on the Mercalli scale is on the low end of the V-VI scale. There would be significant enough shaking to where most people would likely feel it to a degree, possibly introducing some very minor damage, thus increasing the intensity. While Connecticut is inland on the North America plate, making it far from any major plate boundary thus decreasing the risk for any major Earthquake, a quake with enough energy released can expose some vulnerabilities. For example, Connecticut has some cities with larger systems such as New Haven, which can expose some structural and systematic issues. Furthermore, areas such as Branford, while not having any major buildings, overpasses and bridges to come into play. A strong enough quake, ranging in the V range on the Mercalli scale can introduce some minor damage. While all of this is true, while the possibilities are not zero, the risk of significant earthquake damage in Connecticut is low, stemming from the inland positioning on the North American plate and historical data of infrequent and low magnitude quakes.
